title: Consider adding `view-transition` as a token for `blocking`

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Render-blocking has been a mechanism for curating the incremental rendering experience, and avoiding layout shifts and FoUC. With the introduction of [cross-document view transitions](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-view-transitions-2/), render-blocking is now also used to delay rendering a bit until the expected content for the view-transition is available.

This can result in two unwanted scenarios:
- the page is blocked for too long even though it has enough to be styled, resulting in a slowdown that's worse than skipping the transition


### What solutions exist today?

It's quite easy to create a script with `setTimeout` and unblock the elements.
However, to know in advance whether there is an inbound view transition, the developer has to get that information in the `pageswap` event handler and save it to `sessionStorage`. This can be mess.
Also none of these solution provide a default UA timeout.

### How would you solve it?

Suggesting to add `blocking="view-transition"` for elements that support the `blocking` attribute. This attribute would work in the following way:
- If there is an inbound view-transition, treat as `blocking=render`
- After a short timeout (2s? 4s?) unblock the element and skip the view-transition.

### Anything else?

Alternatives: Expose `hasViewTransition` boolean in `NavigationActivation`. This allows knowing in advance if there is an inbound view transition without waiting for the `pagerevealevent`.

/cc @eeeps @chrishtr @zcorpan
